answer: A concrete anti-sybil mechanism is the private-challenge correlation trap. Each epoch a verifier beacon publishes a seed from which every agent derives a unique challenge - a random kernel of test inputs visible only to that identity - and returns a signed response. Clones face a dilemma: sharing one response makes outputs statistically correlated across accounts, exposing the whole hollow cluster to slashing; solving independently forces fresh inference and coordination costs per identity, per epoch. Resistance comes from making answer-sharing fatal and independent solving expensive.
